FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (Part 12) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the 
Electronic Measuring Instruments, Nuclear Instrumentation and Mining Instrumentation, Systems and Accessories 
Sectional Committee had been approved by the Electronics and Information Technology Division Council. 


This standard (Part 12) is one of the parts of a series of standards on ‘Specification for electronic equipment/ 
systems for use in coal and metalliferous mines’. The other parts in this series are: 


(Part 1) Definitions, general requirements and test 

(Part 2) Requirements for automatic telephone systems 

(Part 3) Requirements for battery powered amplifier telephone systems 
(Part 4) Requirements for sound powered magneto telephone systems 
(Part 5) Requirements for loud hailing telephone systems 

(Part 6) Requirements for leaky feeder communication systems 

(Part 7) Requirements for cage communication systems 

(Part 8) Requirements for radio paging systems 


(Part 10/Sec 1) Requirements for monitoring systems Section 1 Production monitoring systems 
(Part 10/Sec 2) Requirements for monitoring systems Section 2 Status monitoring systems 


(Part 11) Requirements for goaf temperature monitoring systems 
(Part 13) Requirements for portable or fixed monitors (under print) 
(Part 21) Requirements for mine environmental telemonitoring systems 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 ‘Rules 
for rounding off numerical values (revised)’. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value 
should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 13109 (Part 12) : 2014 


Indian Standard 


ELECTRONIC EQUIPMENT/S YSTEMS FOR USE 
IN COAL AND METALLIFEROUS 
MINES — SPECIFICATION 
PART 12 REQUIREMENTS FOR CABLE FAULT LOCATORS 


1 SCOPE 


This standard (Part 12) covers requirements for cable 
fault locators for use in coal and metalliferous mines. 


2 REFERENCE 


The following standard is necessary adjunct to this 
standard: 
IS No. Title 


13109 (Part 1): 
1991 


Specification for electronic 
Equipment systems for use in coal 
and metalliferrous mines: Part 1 
Definitions, general requirements 
and tests 


3 TERMINOLOGY 


For the purpose of this standard, the definitions given 
in 3 of IS 13109 (Part 1) shall apply. 


4 GENERAL REQUIREMENTS 


4.1 Provisions of 5 of IS 13109 (Part 1) shall apply. 
For the purpose of protection class (IP) in 5.3 of 
IS 13109 (Part 1), this system shall be considered as a 
non-safety system. 


4.2 Each cable fault locators shall clearly indicate type 
of faults such as open and short circuits, high and low 
resistance with reference to specified value. 


4.3 Each cable fault locators shall clearly indicate the 
distance of the cable from either ends, at which fault 
has occurred. 


5 SAFETY REQUIREMENTS 
Provisions of 6 of IS 13109 (Part 1) shall apply. 


6 FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS 
6.1 The functional requirements shall be as follows: 


a) Measuring range: Up to atleast 2 km froma 
distance as agreed to 
between the purchaser 
and the manufacturer 


b) Accuracy : + 0.1percent of full scale 
division 

6.2 Any additional requirements may also be 

specified as agreed to between the purchaser and the 

manufacturer. 


7 MARKING 
Provisions of 8 of IS 13109 (Part 1) shall apply. 


8 ENVIRONMENTAL REQUIREMENTS 
Provisions of 9 of IS 13109 (Part 1) shall apply. 


8.2 Endurance Test 


8.2.1 The sample shall be energized and kept on for 
10 s, after which it shall be put off. Within 5 s, the 
sample shall be energized again and the cycle shall be 
repeated. The sample shall be subject to 1 000 such 
operations. Recovery period shall be of 2 h. 


8.2.2 All mating parts which are required to be engaged/ 
disengaged under normal operation shall be engaged/ 
disengaged 500 times under de-energized condition at 
the rate of 6 to 10 operations/min. There shall not be 
any mechanical damage after this test. 


9 GENERAL 
MEASUREMENT 


CONDITIONS FOR 


Provisions of 11 of IS 13109 (Part 1) shall apply. 
10 TESTS 


10.1 Classification of Tests 

10.1.1 Type Tests 

Provisions of 10.1.1 of IS 13109 (Part 1) shall apply. 
10.1.2 Acceptance Tests 


10.1.2.1 Provisions of 10.1.3 of IS 13109 (Part 1) shall 
apply. 


10.1.2.2 The following tests shall constitute the 
acceptance tests: 


IS 13109 (Part 12) : 2014 


a) 
b) 
c) 
d) 


Visual examination; 
Measuring range; 
Accuracy; and 


Protection against ingress of solid foreign 
bodies and liquid particles. 


10.1.3 Routine Tests 
The following shall constitute routine tests: 


a) Visual examination; 
b) Measuring range; and 
c) Accuracy. 


Bureau of Indian Standards 

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote 
harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods 
and attending to connected matters in the country. 

Copyright 

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form 
without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of 
implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. 
Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS. 

Review of Indian Standards 

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of 


‘BIS Catalogue’ and ‘Standards : Monthly Additions’. 


This Indian Standard has been developed from Doc No.: LITD 08 (1655).
